summary: All combinations of k distinct digits 1..9 that sum to n.
mainInsight: Backtrack over increasing digits. At each step choose a digit d from start..9, recurse with start = d + 1, and prune when the running sum exceeds n or when the combination reaches length k. A combination is recorded only if its length is k and its sum is n.

approaches.summary: Increasing digits, stop when sum > n or len == k.

edgeCases: n too small or too large

cards.answer: Backtracking over increasing digits 1 to 9, pruning on sum and length. Clue: It asks for every set of k distinct digits from 1 to 9 with a given sum, a tiny pool, so build combinations in increasing order and prune.
keyPoints: It asks for every set of k distinct digits from 1 to 9 with a given sum, a tiny pool, so build combinations in increasing order and prune.
cards.explanation: Only nine digits exist, so enumerating in increasing order with pruning is cheap and gives each set once.

promptVariants: How do you ensure each digit is used at most once and combinations are unique?
What argument does the recursion carry?
options: Recurse with start = d + 1 so digits strictly increase
Sort the digits and use each as many times as needed
Use a visited array and permute all of the digits
Recurse with the same start so digits can repeat
cards.answer: Recurse with start = d + 1 so digits strictly increase

incorrectOptionExplanations.Sort the digits and use each as many tim: Digits can be used only once.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Use a visited array and permute all of t: That would list permutations, not combinations.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Recurse with the same start so digits ca: That allows repeated digits (Combination Sum I).

promptVariants: Which prunings keep the search small?
When can a branch be abandoned?
cards.answer: Stop when the current sum exceeds n or when k digits have been chosen; also skip starts where the remaining digits cannot reach n. Because digits are increasing, once d is too large for the remaining sum, every larger d is too.
keyPoints: Increasing digits allow breaking the loop
cards.explanation: Search space is at most C(9, k).
At most C(9, k) combinations are examined, each costing O(k) to copy.

cards.answer: [[1, 2, 4]]: the only three distinct digits with sum 7
cards.explanation: The minimum sum of three distinct digits is 6; 7 allows only 1 + 2 + 4.
